analysis.title: When Costco Sells Out Of $7,000 Generators, The Fear Is Priced: Goldman's Privorotsky Buys Bonds And AI
key_insights: Goldman's Rich Privorotsky (head of EMEA Delta One trading) says his contrarian muscles are starting to flex on AI. He cites the dollars still to be spent, how far multiples have fallen and what investors are paying for defensives. He says some AI names could go up quickly.

Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8B, above the highest sell-side estimate, and raised its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to 75% from 70%. Its guide was about $130B against roughly $125B expected, with zero China data center compute included. Privorotsky: 'The spending isn't stopping.'

Nvidia shut down hopes that Jensen Huang could return at the top of the call. The stock fell on that line, then ended after hours up almost 5%. NVDA was indicated near $160 premarket, up about 3%, well off the overnight highs and still far below its October record after a 35% plunge.

Goldman's TMT desk says total Nvidia commitments to customers and suppliers rose to $518B from $366B last quarter. The desk reads the call as Kress 'explicitly dialling back the bank of AI role'. That is positive for NVDA CDS/spreads and negative for neoclouds that rely on residual guarantees or offtake support.

Nvidia said guarantees will only apply once projects have land, power, buildings and clear demand. Goldman's credit team estimates $545B of AI project finance in 2027, of which $320B needs a guarantor.
Goldman's TMT desk flags Fed Governor Michael Barr's November 16 speech as a 'clear shift' toward mapping 'the hidden credit plumbing' of the AI buildout.

Privorotsky says much of the recent risk-appetite damage came from a cyber scare after a cluster of outages (Microsoft 365, FAA ground stop, JPMorgan, United, Apple, an Optimizely attack, an NSA internal network outage, an out-of-cycle Oracle patch). WIRED reports no evidence the failures were related or caused by hackers.

Privorotsky calls the retail panic buying of bottled water and generators 'quite a read on sentiment'. He says cyber incidents are rising globally but 'we've hit some local levels of anxiety on the topic'.

The US 3-2-1 crack spread fell 36% in six weeks, from $65.56 to $41.90/bbl. Gasoline and diesel are losing ground to crude even with Hormuz keeping a premium in Brent. API data showed US crude and gasoline stocks each building by about 5m barrels.

Oil geopolitics: the US struck an Iranian missile launch site on Tuesday after Iran said it targeted a US radar installation in Bahrain. Privorotsky sees obvious incentives for a deal nearly nine months in, especially after the midterms, but 'still hard to see a path'.

Metals are weak. London copper is near five-month lows, Shanghai copper is testing 100k, and gold slipped below $3,800 overnight (Goldman's metals desk had $3,763). Goldman's James McGeoch hears margin calls in base and precious metals, with China and CTAs leaning short.
Privorotsky concludes: 'Objectively China tape has been awful. Perhaps commds just telling us policy is way too tight.'

Rates trade: after asking on Monday whether receiving rates is the better expression, Privorotsky now says 'I like long front end bonds alongside equity here'. He sees a meaningful disinflationary impulse if the commodity declines stick, though 'one day isn't a trend'.

Tuesday's tape: high-beta momentum rose, AI outperformed AI losers, the short leg of momentum was hit, and expensive defensives caught down. Privorotsky called this 'somewhat constructive'. The Kospi rebounded 2% and held the prior selloff's lows, and Hynix rose 4%.

Technicals: CTA selling 'may have peaked' in velocity but could still be large if markets stay here, especially in Europe. The S&P closed at 7,340, just below the 200-day at 7,344 (Goldman US trading desk). The Nasdaq broke its early-month lows intraday before recovering into the close.

SK Hynix's blended 24-month forward P/E hit a record-low 1.72x on Tuesday (in a five-year Bloomberg series) and was 1.795x this morning, against a five-year average of 6.9x and a mid-2023 peak of 17x.

Privorotsky says the Hynix multiple should raise worries about earnings sustainability ('cheap get cheaper') but it is hard to press lower, and bearish AI/growth views may be better expressed in other pockets given the margin of safety.
Privorotsky is bearish on a near-term Ukraine ceasefire ahead of Thursday's Trump-Xi-Putin meeting at APEC, especially after reports that Ukraine took out the central road span of the Kerch Bridge.
Privorotsky says that outside of cyber he is struggling to point to a catalyst for the selloff.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman's Privorotsky says Nvidia did 'pretty much everything you could ask for' with a beat and raise ($130B guide vs about $125B expected). The bid faded premarket, and Nvidia is pulling back its guarantee role for customers.
CoreWeave rose 10% after hours following Nvidia's results, despite Goldman's TMT desk saying the dialled-back guarantees are negative for neoclouds reliant on residual guarantees or offtake support.
Nebius rose 10% after hours following Nvidia's results, despite the guarantee pullback flagged by Goldman's TMT desk.

sector_views.rationale: Privorotsky says his contrarian muscles are flexing on AI given the dollars still to be spent and compressed multiples. Hynix trades at a record-low 1.8x forward earnings, and some names 'could go up pretty quickly'.
Privorotsky notes expensive defensives 'had simply gone too far' and finally caught down on Tuesday, which he found somewhat constructive.

sector_views.sector: Commodities (oil products, base and precious metals, grains)
sector_views.rationale: Privorotsky sees commodities rolling over hard enough to deliver a meaningful disinflationary impulse. The crack spread is down 36%, copper is near five-month lows and gold is below $3,800.

earnings_insights: Nvidia (NVDA) reported revenue of $115.8B (reported, already printed overnight), above the highest sell-side estimate. It raised its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to 75% from 70%.
Nvidia guided to about $130B against roughly $125B expected (consensus, per Privorotsky), with zero China data center compute included in the numbers.
Nvidia reported its first quarter without Jensen Huang. The company shut down any hint that Huang could return. The stock ended after hours up almost 5%.

Nvidia's total commitments to customers and suppliers rose to $518B from $366B last quarter (per Goldman's TMT desk), and guarantees will only kick in once projects have land, power, buildings and clear demand.
CoreWeave and Nebius both rose about 10% after hours following Nvidia's results.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Refining margins are deflating as gasoline and diesel lose ground to crude, which supports the commodity disinflation argument.

macro_indicators.reading: Below $3,800 overnight; $3,763 this morning (Goldman metals desk)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Gold cannot hold a bounce even with lower yields. Privorotsky is running out of excuses and suggests a liquidation element.
The index is hanging on to its long-term trend line by a fingernail, a technically fragile position.
Base metals weakness plus a poor China tape is read as a sign policy may be too tight.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Stock builds add to downward pressure on crude and product prices.

trade_ideas.description: Long front-end bonds (receive rates) alongside long equity exposure
trade_ideas.rationale: If commodity declines persist they are a meaningful disinflationary impulse and the front end rallies. If growth holds up, the equity leg works.
trade_ideas.risk: One day is not a trend. The equity leg only works if 1.8x earnings for Hynix is a floor rather than a waypoint.

trade_ideas.description: Contrarian long AI hardware, including SK Hynix, on compressed multiples
trade_ideas.rationale: Large remaining AI spend, multiples have fallen sharply, and investors are paying up for defensives.
trade_ideas.risk: Memory is cyclical and the market may be betting earnings collapse when the AI buildout peaks in 2028 or 2029.

tension_points.bull_case: Privorotsky points to the sheer dollars still to be spent, Nvidia's beat and raise with a $130bn guide, and Hynix at 1.8x forward earnings with a meaningful margin of safety. Some names could rise quickly.
tension_points.bear_case: Cheap can get cheaper if memory earnings collapse once the AI buildout peaks in 2028 or 2029. Nvidia is pulling back its guarantee role, and its best quarter could not hold overnight gains.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The equity leg only works if 1.8x earnings turns out to be a floor rather than a waypoint, meaning Hynix earnings forecasts falling further would invalidate the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: If commodity declines stick, a meaningful disinflationary impulse favors long front-end bonds, and if growth holds up the equity leg does the work.
tension_points.bear_case: Commodity weakness, margin calls in metals and an awful China tape may mean policy is too tight rather than the economy being strong.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Privorotsky says one day is not a trend, so the rates call weakens if the commodity declines do not stick.
